text:
laura: heads up — saw a regression on canary dashboard charts after yesterday's routing policy rollout :eyes:
laura: charts load but theres a ~2s stall before first paint on many dashboards, only on eu-* canaries
laura: repro steps: load /dashboards/alerts, open heatmap, switch to 30d range
laura: attaching quick waterfall: https://img.redwood.internal/wf/1746001234.png
shiv: thanks — do we have a network/parse breakdown? looks like parse/compile is small but main-thread idle + long task at ~1.6s
laura: pasting the devtools snippet:
```
=== waterfall snippet ===
GET /static/chunks/heatmap.3d2f.js  80ms
POST /api/dash/query?routeAffinity=balanced  320ms (backend)
PATCH /api/cache/kv-prefetch  18ms
Main thread: scriptParse 160ms, execute 1300ms, render 40ms
=== end ===
```
mike: routeAffinity=balanced — that rollout changed last night to prefer spare capacity across regions, not affinity. pinging infra.
mike: hypothesis: balanced routing scatters requests off the region's tight kv-cache, so our prefix/KV cache misses spike and runtime has to rebuild large series responses -> big main-thread work
hana: canary metrics show kv-cache hitrate dropped from 92% -> 61% in eu-canaries at the same time as the rollout. perf-bot flagged spike at 13:02 UTC
perf-bot: perf-regression-bot: chart-render p90 increased 1.9x for heatmap on eu-canary between 2025-11-04T12:45 and 2025-11-04T13:05. Linked trace: https://traces.redwood/trace/0a1b2c
shiv: OK. two paths: (A) rollback routing policy to affinity-first for console canaries, (B) quick client mitigation: memoize query results and avoid heavy rehydration on navigation until KV results return
laura: (B) would reduce user-visible flakiness quickly. I can open a tiny client PR: dynamic import heatmap lib and show skeleton while we wait for KV. That avoids the big parse/exec spike.
mike: infra-side I can add a hotfix: prefer local-affinity for internal console traffic via route override for /api/dash/* for 1h. That should restore cache hitrate.
hana: we should also add telemetry to tag requests with routing.variant so we can correlate in future (already added in a feature branch but not sent in canary). please include header `x-rd-routing=variant` in the canary config
laura: created draft branch: `console/heatmap-defer` — will do dynamic import + client memo. small snippets: 
```
// lazy load heatmap
const Heatmap = dynamic(() => import('./Heatmap'), { ssr: false })
const result = useMemo(() => cache.get(queryKey), [queryKey])
```
laura: will open PR in 20m and canary it to eu-canary only
shiv: mike, can you roll the routing override? I think that plus laura's client change should bring p90 back quickly.
mike: rolling override now to eu-canaries only. command: `infractl routes override set --path "/api/dash/*" --policy affinity-local --scope eu-canary --ttl 1h`
mike: override applied, monitoring... :hourglass_flowing_sand:
hana: kv-cache hitrate climbing back to ~88% in metrics, traces show fewer cross-region fetches
perf-bot: perf-regression-bot: p90 heatmap render down to 1.05x baseline at 1746001480
laura: PR opened: https://git.redwood/console/pulls/4123 — small change, no visual diff, just skeleton + lazy import. tagging @shiv @mike for review
shiv: reviewing now. quick note: add a small unit test to ensure skeleton renders when module unresolved, that will catch racey load states
laura: added test, CI green. merging to canary
mike: can we add a short-term dashboard alert: if kv-cache hitrate < 75% and chart p95 > 1.5x baseline -> auto-run the affinity override? probably manual for now, but we should doc the runbook
hana: agreed — I'll draft a runbook and add an observability note to the rollout checklist: ensure `x-rd-routing` header present, and validate kv-cache hitrate before switching to balanced
laura: thanks team — looks like canary is back to normal after the two fixes. follow-ups: (1) telemetry header rollout, (2) longer-term: make chart rendering resilient to cache miss waterfalls (memoization + incremental render), (3) revisit routing policy behavior for internal console traffic
shiv: TL;DR: routing policy change caused cross-region cache misses -> big main-thread rehydrate -> slow charts. Hotfix: route override + client lazy load. Postmortem optional but doc the checklist. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: incident-bot: created incident INC-20251104-heatmap-canary, assigned to eng-platform
laura: adding note to the incident and linking the PR and infra command above
